_readme: THE MAIL TRANSPORT REGISTER — the ONE machine-readable record of how this factory sends mail.
Recorded by Private/decisions/029-email-sending-architecture.md (ADR 029).
🔴 WHY IT EXISTS — a false 🔴🔴 store-submission blocker, 2026-08-03/04.
An audit agent concluded that Supabase Auth could not deliver mail to real users and escalated it
to a blocker. It had read FOUR repo documents that all agreed with each other. Every one of them
was stale, and SUPABASE_PAT — the credential that can read the real state in one GET — sat in the
vault the entire time. Four agreeing documents are not evidence; they are one stale fact copied
four times. So the fact now has ONE home, in a file a machine can parse, instead of N prose copies
that drift independently and reinforce each other while they do it.
THE ALLOCATION RULE (ADR 029 §1): Workspace = the owner's mailbox · Resend = everything a machine
sends. The split is by DOMAIN so it cannot be fudged: nikatru.com is Workspace and carries human
mail only; mail.nikatru.com is Resend and carries every automated message, for every app.
ONE POOLED SUBDOMAIN, NOT ONE PER APP (ADR 029 §2). Splitting a 50-app factory into 50 sending
subdomains yields 50 identifiers permanently stuck at 'unknown', which receivers treat as similar
to bad. App identity goes in the DISPLAY NAME, not the domain. The invariants below encode that:
exactly one machine-mail rail, and its domain must sit UNDER the mailbox domain.
WHAT READS THIS FILE.
· tooling/ci/assert-mail-transport-claims.mjs   OFFLINE. Runs in ci.yml. Checks the invariants
below hold, and that no document in the corpus restates the OLD transport without also stating
the current one. It holds no credential, so it CANNOT see live drift.
· tooling/ops/verify-supabase-templates.mjs     LIVE. Reads the real Supabase config with
SUPABASE_PAT and reports drift against `supabaseAuth` below and against the DR templates.
Scheduled in ops-watch.yml when the repo secret exists; prints the gap loudly when it does not.
⚠️ NOTHING HERE IS SELF-VERIFYING. `supabaseAuth` records what a GET returned on `verifiedLiveOn`.
It is a RECORD of a reading, not the reading. Only the live checker can tell you it is still true.
🔴 READ-ONLY AGAINST SUPABASE, ALWAYS. `PATCH /v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth` REPLACES the auth
config instead of merging it. On 2026-08-04 a one-field PATCH emptied the whole SMTP block, reset
rate_limit_email_sent 100 → 2, and reverted all three branded templates to Supabase defaults. If
you must write, GET the full config first and send it back COMPLETE.
⏱ APPENDED 2026-09-16 — THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS LEFT EXACTLY AS WRITTEN, and its ADVICE IS NOW THE
DANGEROUS ONE. Both halves were re-measured today, on this project, before any hardening write:
(a) PATCH MERGES. A deliberate one-field probe body, `{"password_min_length": 8}`, was sent and
the whole config re-GET and diffed field by field against the reading taken minutes earlier:
EXACTLY 1 of 243 fields changed. The SMTP block, rate_limit_email_sent and all three branded
templates were untouched, and `verify-supabase-templates.mjs` re-ran IN SYNC immediately
after. The nine remaining hardening fields then went in the same way: 10 of 243 changed, all
ten the decided ones. Whatever happened on 2026-08-04, a one-field PATCH does not do it today.
(b) SENDING THE FULL BODY BACK WOULD DESTROY THE SMTP PASSWORD. `GET config/auth` returns a
`smtp_pass` of 64 characters; the real credential in the vault is 36. It is not a row of
asterisks, so it does not LOOK masked — it looks like a value, and a full-body round trip
would write that opaque 64-character string in as the password. The advice above is what
would have caused that.
⇒ The rule is now: WRITE THE FIELDS YOU MEAN, then GET the whole config back and DIFF it against
the reading you took first. The diff is the control; the body shape is not. Never round-trip a
field whose value the API will not give you back.

rails.why: Receives everything; the owner replies by hand. It sends NOTHING automated, so the account-suspension blast radius — this account owns Play Console, Microsoft Partner Center and Apple — never applies to mail sent to strangers.
Everything a machine sends, for every app: auth mail, error alerts, later receipts and newsletter. One pooled identifier that can actually earn a reputation.

supabaseAuth._why: The shared identity project authenticates every app in the portfolio, so its transport is the portfolio's transport. Values below were READ from GET /v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth on verifiedLiveOn. smtp_pass is deliberately absent — it is a secret and lives in .claude/secrets.env.
_whyHardening: ⏱ 2026-09-16 — the ten fields after `mailer_autoconfirm` are the password/session hardening the
owner ruled on 2026-09-15 (OWNER_QUEUE S-9, register O-AUTH-PASSWORD-RESET-HARDENING: "Turn all
on"). They are recorded HERE, beside the transport, because this file is the one record the live
checker reads and Ops watch's "The live auth config still matches what the repo recorded" job is
the only thing that can see them drift back.
Every key below is a LIVE Supabase field name, read back from a GET after the PATCH landed on
2026-09-16. `transport` is the one exception and is NOT a live field — it is this register's own
vocabulary for what the SMTP block adds up to, which is why the checker excludes it by name.

_why: The phrases the four stale documents used. They are NOT banned — the incident is worth recording
and ADR 029, PROJECT_STATE.md and the two Supabase guards all describe the old state ON PURPOSE.
A guard that forbade the words outright would fail on correct input, and a guard that fails on
correct input gets deleted by whoever hits it next.
The rule is instead: a unit of text that states the OLD transport must ALSO state the current
one. A Markdown section is the unit, because a reader who lands on a section reads that section;
for everything else the unit is the file. Each of the four documents that caused the incident
carried the old claim with no correction anywhere in the file — all four would have failed.
Patterns are matched case-insensitively. `correctionMarkers` is what satisfies the rule.

patterns.why: Supabase's own name for the shared sender that only delivers to project team members. We have not been on it since custom SMTP was configured; it was true for a few minutes on 2026-08-04 when a one-field PATCH wiped the config.
The phrase all four stale documents used. It was the load-bearing inference behind the false store-submission blocker.

From Supabase's 400 on template edits — `Email template modification is not available for free tier projects using the default email provider`. Quoted as a live blocker in three plan files; the templates have been branded and applied all along.

patterns.pattern: refuse[sd]? to deliver messages to addresses
patterns.why: Supabase's documented behaviour WITHOUT custom SMTP. Quoted as a statement about this project, which is what turned a doc-reading into a blocker.
The credentials were handed over and configured before any of these files claimed otherwise. smtp_pass reads SET on the live project.

correctionMarkers.why: Naming the live SMTP host IS stating the current transport.
Naming the machine-mail domain states which rail sends automated mail.
The decision record that carries the retraction and the full reasoning.
The ADR's path, for links and cross-references.

liveChecker.why: The only thing that can see drift between this record and the live project. The CI guard asserts it still READS this file — a live checker that hardcodes its expectations stops being a checker of this record and becomes a second copy of it, which is the defect this register exists to remove.
